topics.title: Flood Safety
topics.subtitle: Stay safe before, during and after flooding

sections.title: Move to higher ground
sections.body: If flooding is imminent, move to the highest point in your building or evacuate to elevated terrain. Avoid basements and underground car parks.
steps: Take your emergency kit, phone and charger.
Switch off electricity and gas if it is safe to do so.
Help children, older people and neighbours who need assistance.
Follow official evacuation routes from the DMC.

sections.title: Never cross floodwater
sections.body: Just 15 centimetres of moving water can knock an adult down, and 30 centimetres can float a small car. Floodwater may hide open drains, debris and live electrical wires.
steps: Turn around and choose a higher route.
Do not swim, walk or drive through water.
Keep away from riverbanks, canals and storm drains.
If your vehicle stalls in water, abandon it and move to higher ground.

sections.title: Inside your home
sections.body: Move valuables, documents and medicines above expected flood level. Fill clean containers with drinking water in case supply is cut.
steps: Unplug appliances and move them higher.
Close doors and place sandbags or towels at low entry points.
Keep listening to official alerts and local radio.
Do not touch electrical switches while standing in water.

sections.title: After the water recedes
sections.body: Floodwater can be contaminated with sewage and chemicals. Clean and disinfect everything that was touched by floodwater and watch for structural damage.
steps: Wait for authorities to say it is safe to return.
Wear boots and gloves while cleaning.
Discard food that touched floodwater.
Photograph damage for insurance and support applications.

topics.title: Landslide Safety
topics.subtitle: Recognise warning signs in hilly terrain

sections.title: Warning signs
sections.body: Watch for new cracks in the ground, doors or windows that stick, tilting trees or utility poles, and muddy water emerging from slopes.
steps: Listen for rumbling or cracking sounds.
Check for sudden changes in springs or streams.
Report new cracks or slope movement to local authorities.
Be extra alert during and after heavy rain.

sections.title: Evacuate early
sections.body: If you suspect a landslide, leave immediately. Do not wait for official confirmation if you see or hear active slope movement.
steps: Move away from the slope and out of the path of debris.
Avoid valleys, channels and the base of hills.
Warn neighbours as you leave.
Call 117 and report your location.

sections.title: If escape is not possible
sections.body: Move to the upper floor of a sturdy building and stay away from outside walls. Protect your head with a helmet, cushion or thick clothing.
steps: Curl into a tight ball and protect your head.
Stay under a strong table or interior wall.
Do not use lifts.
Stay put until it is safe to move.

topics.title: Cyclone & Storms
topics.subtitle: Prepare for high winds and heavy rain

sections.title: Before the storm
sections.body: Secure loose outdoor items, trim overhanging branches and charge phones and power banks. Store drinking water and non-perishable food.
steps: Bring in bins, furniture and garden equipment.
Close and reinforce windows and doors.
Charge devices and keep a torch ready.
Know the nearest safe shelter.

sections.title: During the storm
sections.body: Stay indoors and away from windows. Avoid using wired electrical equipment and do not go outside during the calm eye of a cyclone.
steps: Move to an interior room on the lowest floor.
Stay away from glass and external walls.
Do not go outside until authorities say it is safe.
Keep listening to official updates.

sections.title: After the storm
sections.body: Watch for downed power lines, weakened trees and flooded roads. Avoid damaged buildings and report hazards to authorities.
steps: Treat every power line as live.
Do not enter damaged structures.
Boil or purify drinking water if supply is uncertain.
Help neighbours and share verified information.

topics.title: Tsunami Safety
topics.subtitle: Act fast when the coast is at risk

sections.title: Natural warning signs
sections.body: A strong earthquake near the coast, a sudden rise or fall in sea level, or a loud ocean roar can be a natural tsunami warning. Do not wait for an official alert.
steps: Move inland and to higher ground immediately.
Leave beaches, harbours and river mouths.
Do not return to the coast to watch.
Warn others as you move.

sections.title: Reach high ground
sections.body: Go to a designated evacuation site at least 20 metres above sea level or 2 kilometres inland. If you cannot leave, move to the upper floor of a reinforced building.
steps: Follow tsunami evacuation signs.
Avoid bridges and coastal roads.
Stay there until officials give the all-clear.
Keep your phone and emergency kit with you.

sections.title: After the wave
sections.body: Tsunami waves can continue for hours and later waves may be larger. Only return when authorities confirm it is safe.
steps: Stay away from flooded and damaged areas.
Watch for debris, live wires and contaminated water.
Check on vulnerable neighbours.
Follow official information channels.

topics.title: Fire Safety
topics.subtitle: Escape safely and reduce smoke exposure

sections.title: If a fire starts
sections.body: Raise the alarm, get everyone out and call 110. Never re-enter a burning building for possessions.
steps: Shout to alert others.
Leave by the nearest safe exit.
Close doors behind you to slow the fire.
Call 110 from a safe place.

sections.title: Escaping smoke
sections.body: Smoke is more dangerous than flames. Stay low, cover your nose and mouth with a cloth and feel doors before opening them.
steps: Crawl below the smoke layer.
Do not open a hot door.
Use stairs, never a lift.
If trapped, seal gaps and signal from a window.

sections.title: Clothing on fire
sections.body: Stop, drop and roll. Smother the flames with a heavy blanket if available and cool burns with running water.
steps: Stop moving and drop to the ground.
Roll to smother the flames.
Remove smouldering clothing carefully.
Seek medical help for burns.

topics.title: First Aid Basics
topics.subtitle: Simple steps that can save a life

sections.title: Check the scene
sections.body: Before helping, make sure the area is safe for you and the injured person. Call 1990 for an ambulance when needed.
steps: Look for traffic, fire, water or electrical hazards.
Call 1990 and give a clear location.
Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger.
Ask bystanders to help direct emergency services.

sections.title: Severe bleeding
sections.body: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth. Keep pressing and do not remove the cloth if it soaks through.
steps: Press firmly on the wound.
Add more cloth on top if needed.
Elevate the limb if possible.
Keep the person warm and calm.

sections.title: CPR
sections.body: If a person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, start chest compressions and call for help.
steps: Place the heel of your hand in the centre of the chest.
Push hard and fast at about 100 to 120 compressions per minute.
Allow the chest to come back up between compressions.
Continue until help arrives or the person recovers.

topics.title: Emergency Kit
topics.subtitle: Pack what you need before disaster strikes

sections.title: Water and food
sections.body: Keep at least three days of supplies for every person in your household. Choose food that does not need cooking.
steps: Three litres of drinking water per person per day.
Ready-to-eat food and a manual can opener.
Baby formula or pet food if needed.
Water purification tablets or a filter.

sections.title: Light and power
sections.body: Power may be cut for days. Keep torches, batteries and a power bank in a waterproof bag.
steps: Torch and spare batteries.
Fully charged power bank and charging cable.
Battery or hand-crank radio.
Glow sticks for children.

sections.title: Documents and health
sections.body: Store copies of important documents and enough medicine for at least a week.
steps: ID, insurance and property documents in a waterproof pouch.
Prescription medicines and a basic first aid kit.
Emergency contact list on paper.
Cash in small notes.
